headline: Across media, gaming, publishing and education, firms show mixed financial results but a common push toward digital and AI initiatives.
summary: Media & Entertainment companies report solid revenue growth, especially Disney, while tightening IT spend and cutting costs. Gaming firms are split, with Caesars losing money and Bally's expanding digital platforms and financing. Publishing sees mixed outcomes as Pearson grows and Scholastic struggles, yet AI tools are being rolled out. Education players are investing heavily in AI and quantum research, with Pearson leading revenue growth.

industries.summary: Disney posted 7% revenue growth and strong operating margin. Warner Bros. Discovery/Skydance raised its EBITDA outlook despite a revenue dip. Versant reaffirmed guidance with modest growth. Cost‑cutting and AI projects dominate the agenda.

leaders.why: Revenue of $25,248 m and 7% YoY growth

themes.title: AI & tech investment
themes.detail: Disney filed a patent for real‑time AI character interactions; other firms are embedding AI in data platforms.

themes.title: Cost‑cutting
themes.detail: Layoffs and restructuring aim for up to 20% cost savings across the sector.

industries.it_note: IT budgets are being trimmed as firms focus on selective AI projects and efficiency gains.

industries.summary: Caesars posted a $2.94 bn revenue but widened its net loss. Bally's delivered 20% revenue growth and new financing for casino sites. Light & Wonder and Brightstar show stable or neutral performance with cashless payment rollouts.

laggards.why: Widened GAAP net loss of $123 m

themes.title: Digital platform rebuild
themes.detail: New online casino and sportsbook platforms are being launched and expanded.

themes.title: Financing for tech infrastructure
themes.detail: $560 m and $400 m financings signal upcoming technology builds for new casino sites.

industries.it_note: Investments in digital casino platforms and cashless payment systems indicate growing IT spend.

industries.summary: Pearson accelerated revenue to $1,779 m and cut profit guidance, while Scholastic missed revenue and widened losses. Wolters Kluwer remains neutral but is expanding AI tools. AI and digital upgrades are a common thread.

leaders.why: Revenue of $1,779 m and expanding AI tutoring

laggards.why: Revenue miss of $216.8 m and -42.5% operating margin

themes.title: AI & tech investment
themes.detail: CCH Axcess, Expert AI, and Career Studios launch AI‑driven tools for tax, legal and adult learning.

industries.it_note: Publishers are increasing AI‑focused development to modernize content creation and delivery.

industries.summary: Pearson shows strong revenue growth and AI‑tutor launches. NYU secures multiple $30 m+ investments for quantum and AI research. SLU adds AI focus through a partnership with World Wide Technology. Overall tech spend is rising.

leaders.why: Revenue of $1,779 m and AI‑driven Career Studios

laggards.why: Outsourced custodial services, indicating cost focus

themes.title: AI research and partnerships
themes.detail: NYU builds AI for archaeology and student interaction; SLU partners with WWT to add AI capabilities.

themes.title: Quantum and advanced tech investment
themes.detail: NYU receives multi‑$30 m investments for a quantum fabrication facility.

industries.it_note: Education institutions are accelerating AI and quantum initiatives, driving higher IT budgets.
